restrictions: time_log2 = 118.11514 is log2 of (W_BUDGET + R + 6 B) / 2812 + 2^36 target-compressions, with W_BUDGET = floor(B x 523,024,054 x (1 + 2^-20)) + 1 = 1012080500635223110840692577911591778473 = 2^129.5725 from 99% bounds: 523,024,054 ops/window and the direct distinct-group endpoint g- = 50,394.88 groups/window (the cent-floor of the direct 99% endpoint 50,394.8847 over the 24 windows, introduced by 69616879, credited; the older product path c- r- = 50,388.97 is no longer used) (proof Section 7). 10,263.1 ops/claw over 24 windows of 2^26 walk evaluations on the real step function (1,213,630 claws, 1,211,719 groups; Section 5, Appendix A). G = ln(1/0.60999) / (p8 p9 2^-32 p_tail) = 2^116.2312 groups, p8 p9 = 585/524288, log2 p_tail = -75.44 (Section 8). Halts: B = floor(G (1 + 2^-19) / g-) + 1 = 1935053517521326091190654730241 = 2^100.6102 windows or W_BUDGET = 2^129.5725 operations (Section 7); all other halts charged. Unconditional success probability >= (1 - 0.60999) - 2 exp(-2^17.5) > 0.390009 > 0.39.

Construction, credited: sraiw's 38912d66 transplants the published Table 23 pair of ePrint 2026/1120 onto a random first-block chaining value through an exact bijection (cv, a0, a1) <-> (W8, W9, W16..W23); row 16 is the claw F(a0) = F(u), a0 even and u odd, of a 32-bit map, found by a van Oorschot-Wiener distinguished-point walk (dariolina's row-16 claw idea: 21b6653a, 2c48b18c, cfe5c4e2, 4e396742); then W8 in F8 and W9 in F9 (exact 585/524288), W17 = the published value (2^-32 for uniform W17), and the tail rows 18 to 38 (p_tail). Declared dependencies: 44870635 (lamb356, the base program), d90878ff (Jbenisek, the machine program), 38912d66, 4e396742, 2c48b18c, cfe5c4e2, 744875ec, 0c1ef7c3, 6b678689.

Machine model (prices of this entry's cost model, proof Section 4), collision-frontier-v5: a counted 256-bit word RAM with 256 registers (counted as memory), 2812 operations per target compression. One operation each: XOR, AND, OR, NOT, move, shift, rotate, add, subtract, compare, set; a branch is a compare plus a branch (2); a load or a store is 3 (index shift, base add, access); a call plus its return is 2. A walk-kernel body record (register-to-register XOR, AND, OR or NOT, no immediate operand) is 5 bytes, the price of dariolina's 6b678689 and Jbenisek's 0c1ef7c3; every other instruction is 36 bytes. One executed WebAssembly operator of the in-program generator is one operation (it halts at 575,000 operators). Every operation of the program is counted by the class Mach; no price is an average.

Machine: the parent's word-RAM convention (dariolina 744875ec; Jbenisek 3c1d7f68, 368d1718, 01e31be9), unchanged; the two participant programs are byte-identical to 7c4da9b7's except the two halt constants B = 1935053517521326091190654730241 and W_BUDGET = 1012080500635223110840692577911591778473, the packed EXP table (this entry's 14 fresh organizer runs at ids r39-tail2-01..14), the declaration constants (QDECL = -75.44, the three prior-set constants P448/P190/P7C4) and the pooled verification code of verify_smc_stats(). time_log2 = 118.11514 (exact 118.11514 at five decimals) is log2 of (W_BUDGET + R + 6 B) / 2812 + 2^36 (proof Section 7); memory, preprocessing (2^36), advice (160 bytes) and the success probability are unchanged from the parent.

Memory 1,047,892 bytes = 2^19.9991, claimed as 2^20: register file 8,192; 2 kernel images x 780 x 5 = 7,800; 3,599 other instructions (734 census, 1,100 hand-counted routines, 1,765 generator and relocation) x 36 = 129,564; table 26,112 words x 32 = 835,584; lane array, save area, queue, pair slots, timing wheel, free stack and counters 66,592; advice 160. The generator's scratch lies in the table region during generation. No solver, no search campaign and no preprocessing buffer: setup and the program share this peak.

Advice and preprocessing (H3-advice-construction, proof Section 11, the form of 38912d66 Section 4.2): the base is the published Table 23 pair of ePrint 2026/1120 (chaining value, M, M': 160 bytes), embedded as advice. The program reads from it only the dense part of the characteristic (states of steps 2 to 15, W10..W15, D8, D9, g, the row-17 value). Its construction takes at most 2^36 target-compressions in at most 2^16 bytes of resident memory: 2^34 candidates on steps 10 to 15 (384 state bits under 350 conditions; steps 9 down to 0 and CV_PUB follow by exact downward step inversion with zero branching), each tested for non-empty row-16 and row-17 fibres by exact 32-bit bit-by-bit DFS (solve_row_exact) in under 2^2 compressions per candidate (verified in r39-transplant-claw trial 0). The paper's Step 1 is about 2^34.2 SHA-256 calls and its Step 2 holds with probability 1.

Experiments r39-transplant-claw and r39-window-small run experiments/r39joint.py in the organizer sandbox with hard assert verification of all outputs: r39-transplant-claw (trial 0: the published pair through claw() plus verify_advice_construction() running solve_row_exact on rows 16 and 17, downward step inversion, and a 256-candidate step-15 slice; trials 1..255: the transplant identity on 255 random chaining values) and r39-window-small (trials 0..3: 4 independent windows of 2^22 evaluations = 2^24 total, 3,265 distinct claws and groups, WIN_EXP counts, chi-square and autocorrelation checks). The tail is replicated by experiments/r39tail.py v3 (r39-tail2-01..14, asserting the packed EXP table, this set's linear mean above QDECL, and the pooled four-set 99.9% Satterthwaite bound above QDECL = -75.44; proof Sections 8 and 10).

heuristics.statement: Four parts. (a) The chaining value cv of a random first block behaves as an independent random value for the walk map F and the later events, so the windows of the program are independent trials. (b) The yield and the cost of a window are those measured on the real step function over 24 full-size windows: 50,567.92 distinct claws, 50,488.29 distinct claw groups and 10,263.1 operations per distinct claw (one-sided 99% bounds mu+ = 523,024,054 operations, c- = 50,472.66 claws, g- = 50,394.89 groups, r- = 0.998342 groups/claw); the program cannot be run for 2^100.70 windows. (c) A distinct claw (a0 even, u odd, F(a0) = F(u)) is, for the events W8 in F8, W9 in F9, W17 = 0x71e9ba98 and the tail, a trial with probability p8 p9 2^-32 p_tail, independent of the walk's yield, with p8 p9 = 585/524288 exact; claws are counted by groups with a shared endpoint (one claw per group suffices). (d) W17 is uniform over the claws.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r39-prefix-v1 and the program of experiments/r39joint.py: first blocks drawn uniformly, windows of 2^26 walk evaluations of the real step function F, claws with W16 = g by the published construction. Not claimed for another base pair, another round count or another walk.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory: walk claws are uniform on the free words of the bijection (cv, a0, a1) <-> (W8, W9, W16..W23) apart from the claw equation. Directly verified in the organizer sandbox by hard asserts in r39joint.py (r39-window-small trials 0..3, 4 windows = 2^24 walk evaluations, 3,265 distinct claws and 3,265 groups in WIN_EXP): W9 in F9 55 (51.8 expected), W8 in F8 224 (229.6), joint F9 & F8 2 (3.64), W17 low-8 matches 11 (12.75), low-12 matches 2 (0.80), and 256-bin chi-square of W17 mod 256 is 239.57 (255 df) and W18 mod 256 is 248.67 (255 df). Also measured on 310,224 claws of 6 first blocks: W9 in F9 5,015 (0.01617 vs 0.01587), W8 in F8 22,002 (0.07092 vs 0.07031), both 360 (0.001160 vs 0.001116); W17 low-k matches k=8: 1,199 (1,211.8), k=12: 82 (75.7), k=16: 5 (4.73), low-16 chi-square 65,830.2 (65,535 df, z=0.82). Part (b) is measured over 24 full windows (Appendix A, 9,975.9..10,521.9 ops/claw, SE 31.8; g- = 50,394.89) and extended to 2^100.6102 windows by (a).
heuristics.limitations: The organizer sandbox runs 4 windows of 2^22 evaluations (3,265 distinct claws/groups, asserting WIN_EXP, W8/W9 rates, W17 low-8/12 matches, and 256-bin chi-square uniformity of W17 and W18 low bytes) and the offline check covers 24 full windows (1,213,630 claws, SE 0.31% = 0.004 bit) and 310,224 claws on the low 16 bits of W17; uniformity of the high 16 bits of W17 and extrapolation from 24 full windows to 2^100.6102 windows are parts (a)-(d).

heuristics.statement: For the claws of the program (a0 even, u odd, W16 = g, W8 in F8, W9 in F9, W17 = 0x71e9ba98) the probability that the two 39-step compressions of the pair give equal 256-bit outputs is at least 2^-75.44 for the quantity of proof Section 8 (rows 18 to 38, W18..W23 uniform; the four parity classes of (a0, u) fall with exact probability 1/4 each; pooling them presumes their exchangeability for the collision event, declared here, while the class-specific estimator 4 * hits_(even, odd) / n is exactly unbiased with no premise and its mean over this entry's runs is -75.3875, above the declared value), a lower bound on the tail probability because the carrier K_P is a subset of all routes to a collision. The declared value is the pre-registered pooled rule: 0.01 below the one-sided 99.9% Satterthwaite lower bound of the inverse-variance pooled log-scale mean over four public run sets of the same unbiased estimator (4487063's 14, 19034ce's 14, 7c4da9b7's 14, this entry's 14 fresh runs), rounded down.
heuristics.scope: The tail rows 18 to 38 of the Table 23 trail after the claw, W8 uniform on F8, W9 uniform on F9, E18..E23 of the first member uniform on 2^32, a0 even and u odd, estimated by the v2 work allocation (800 particles, balanced stage lanes, 3,276,800 proposals per run). Not claimed for another trail or allocation.
heuristics.extrapolation: Our theory: p_tail >= 2^-75.44. The organizer replica experiments/r39tail.py v3 (r39-tail2-01..14, 800 particles, stage lanes 8x512/8x2048/8x2048/4x128/6x256/1x4, 20 trials x 80 batches x 2048 proposals = 3,276,800 proposals per run) hard-asserts EXP and verify_smc_stats() on every run: 3,467 verified collisions in 45,875,200 proposals across the 14 public-seed runs, parity classes [870, 840, 886, 871] (chi-square 1.29 on 3 df). By Del Moral's Feynman-Kac theorem the unnormalized product estimator Q'_r = 2^(l2_r) * (hits_r / 3276800) is exactly unbiased on the linear scale. This entry's set: n = 14, log-mean -75.3469, sd 0.1518. Pooled with the three prior public sets at their published constants (4487063: n = 14, log2 linear mean -75.3927, linear 99% bound -75.5916; 19034ce: n = 14, -75.3284, -75.5062; 7c4da9b7: n = 14, log mean -75.2586, sd 0.1834; the linear-scale constants converted to the log scale by the documented delta-method identities inside the program): pooled log-mean -75.3297, se 0.0270, Satterthwaite df 41, one-sided 99.9% bound (t = 3.385) -75.42104 > QDECL = -75.44. Pooling is valid and conservative: same unbiased estimator of the same quantity, no shared seeds, and E[log2 Q'] <= log2 E[Q'] (Jensen), so the pooled log-scale lower bound bounds the declared quantity. The rule was frozen before this entry's runs (six private-seed sizing runs, mean -75.3736, sd 0.1695; the rule from the three public sets alone declares -75.45); dropping any one set still bounds at least the predecessor's -75.47 (-75.4147 / -75.4244 / -75.4700 / -75.4384). Cross-checks: an offline C run (64 seeds x 2^28 samples) gives -75.354 and sraiw's bound is -75.4278 (38912d66), both above the declared value. The v2 program reproduces 19034ce byte-identically at 19034ce's parameters, so the estimator semantics are unchanged from the accepted 4487063.
heuristics.limitations: A one-sided 99.9% Satterthwaite confidence lower bound (-75.42104, pooled inverse-variance over four public run sets, 0.019 bits above the declared -75.44; weights 0.11/0.14/0.30/0.44, so no single set dominates; without 7c4da9b7's set the bound is exactly the predecessor's -75.47, disclosed). The prior sets' constants are quoted from their public submissions and regenerable from their public programs and seeds; their conversion to the log scale uses the delta-method identities (documented, and checked against 7c4da9b7's directly published log-scale values). Stage 18 is calibrated against direct uniform Monte Carlo (c18 = 206/65536, asserted); K_P is a subset of all collision routes so Q <= p_tail. The 14 runs are public-seed replays without a holdout, as in the accepted 4487063; the pre-registration protocol (rule frozen from public prior sets plus private sizing runs before any new organizer run) addresses the coverage finding F-EXP-TAIL-COVERAGE of c30c0d70.

heuristics.statement: Constructing the 160-byte Table 23 base pair (ePrint 2026/1120, Section 4.3; sraiw 38912d66 Section 4.2) takes at most 2^36 target-compressions (preprocessing_log2 = 36) in at most 2^16 bytes of resident memory: on steps 10 to 15, the 384 state bits under the 350 Table 23 differential and carry conditions leave a 2^34-candidate space (steps 9 down to 0 and CV_PUB are uniquely determined downward by step inversion with zero search), and each candidate is tested for non-empty row-16 fibre G16 and row-17 fibre G17(g) by exact 32-bit bit-by-bit DFS (solve_row_exact) in under 2^2 = 4 target-compressions (11,248 word operations) per candidate.
heuristics.scope: One-time offline construction of the 160-byte advice (CV_PUB, M_PUB, MP_PUB) for sha256-r39-prefix-v1; not part of the online walk.
heuristics.extrapolation: Trials 0 and 1 of experiment:r39-transplant-claw execute verify_advice_construction() in experiments/r39joint.py: it runs the exact 32-bit bit-by-bit DFS fibre solver solve_row_exact on rows 16 and 17 of the Table 23 base (verifying g16_fibre_size = 2 with G16 = 0xbca1c321, g17_fibre_size = 1 with W17 = 0x71e9ba98, and fibre_dfs_ops = 1944 < 2812 word operations < 1 target-compression), verifies that steps 9 down to 0 and CV_PUB are uniquely recovered from steps 10 to 15 and W[0..15] by exact downward step inversion with zero search (downward_inv_ok = 1), and enumerates a 256-candidate local slice of the step-15 free bits (advice_slice_cands = 256, advice_slice_hits = 1, ops_per_cand = 408 < 4 * 2812 word operations < 2^2 target-compressions). Extrapolated from the 256-candidate slice and the ePrint 2026/1120 Section 4.3 Step 1 measurement (about 2^34.2 SHA-256 calls, Step 2 probability 1) to the 2^34-candidate space on steps 10 to 15.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer sandbox runs the exact row-16/row-17 DFS fibre enumeration, exact downward step inversion on steps 13..0, and a 256-candidate step-15 slice rather than the full 2^34-candidate enumeration; the 2^34 candidate count and 2^34.2 SHA-256 calls come from the 384 - 350 = 34 free bits on steps 10 to 15 of Table 23 and ePrint 2026/1120 Section 4.3. Because the benchmark scalar is log2(T_online + T_pre) with T_online = 2^118.11514, any preprocessing cost up to 2^98 target-compressions adds less than 2^-20 to T_online and leaves the rounded scalar time_log2 = 118.11514 unchanged.

heuristics.statement: Distinct claw groups of the run (claws grouped into connected components by shared endpoint; distinct groups have disjoint inputs (a0, u) of the bijection), within a window and across windows, are independent trials for the events W8 in F8, W9 in F9, W17 = 0x71e9ba98 and the tail, so the run succeeds with conditional probability 1 - (1 - p_claw)^G >= 1 - exp(-G p_claw) = 0.390010 over G = 2^116.2312 groups (and unconditional probability >= 0.390010 - 2 exp(-2^17.5) > 0.390009 > 0.39 after the Hoeffding bound).
heuristics.scope: The amplification of proof Section 7 over the G = 2^116.2312 groups of the fixed target sha256-r39-prefix-v1 and the program experiments/r39joint.py; not claimed for another walk or round count.
heuristics.extrapolation: Across windows the chaining value is fresh (H1(a)). Directly verified in the organizer sandbox by hard asserts in r39joint.py (r39-window-small trials 0..3, 4 windows = 2^24 evaluations): 3,265 distinct claw groups in 3,265 distinct claws (807, 827, 795, 836; ratio 1.0000), 100% distinct (W8, W9, W17, W18) tuples per window, 256-bin chi-square of W17 mod 256 is 239.57 (255 df) and first tail word W18 mod 256 is 248.67 (255 df), and lag-1 group autocorrelation across consecutive groups is < 0.02 for W9 in F9 (-0.0165), W17[0] (0.0116), and W18[0] (0.0020). Across all 24 full windows (Appendix A): 1,211,719 distinct groups in 1,213,630 claws (mean 50,488.29, sd 183.04, 99% lower bound g- = 50,394.89; ratio 0.998425, 99% lower bound r- = 0.998342, c- r- = 50,388.97 <= g-), binomial F9/F8 counts (chi-square 22.6 and 32.0 on 24 df), and F9 lag-1 autocorrelation within 0.012.
heuristics.limitations: Within-window independence across distinct claw groups is tested in the organizer sandbox on 3,265 groups (100% distinct (W8, W9, W17, W18) tuples, 256-bin chi-square uniformity of W17 and first tail word W18 low bytes, and lag-1 group autocorrelation < 0.02 for F9, W17[0], and W18[0]) and across 24 full windows (1,211,719 groups); full 32-bit W17 and 39-step tail independence across groups beyond low-byte and lag-1 tests is the remaining extrapolation.
